recreation_prompt_markdown:
Create a polished mobile-first browser game called **Golden Abyss: Infinite Catch**. The game should run as a single HTML page with a full-screen canvas playfield and layered DOM UI. The player controls an abyss-fishing vessel floating near the surface of a dark futuristic ocean. Use one elegant input model: when the player holds or presses on the canvas, the hook descends straight down; when the player releases, the hook reels back up toward the boat. The hook always stays aligned to the boat horizontally, so the fun comes from choosing when to dive, how deep to go, and how many fish to snag before the hook returns.

Build the main loop around endless catch-and-upgrade play. Fish of different rarity, color, size, speed, and depth range should swim horizontally across the screen. Shallow layers contain common fish, while deeper layers unlock rarer, more valuable-looking species. The player’s hook can catch fish on contact while descending or hovering, but it has a limited carrying capacity; once full, or once the player releases, it rises back to the surface and deposits the haul. Every successful return should increment a visible catch total and trigger satisfying positive feedback such as floating `+1` text, spark particles, a short sound effect, and a compact animated catch notification.

Present the game with a striking gold-and-teal sci-fi abyss aesthetic. The background should use layered deep-ocean gradients, subtle drifting particles, depth markers, glowing UI borders, and a premium arcade look. Include a dramatic start screen with the title “Golden Abyss” and subtitle “Infinite Catch,” a hero illustration of the catcher craft, a short description of the controls, and a prominent launch button. Once launched, show a top HUD with budget, current depth, and catch count. Add a bottom “deck console” shop panel with large touch-friendly buttons and two tabs: **Gear** and **Crew**.

The Gear tab should upgrade three core systems: maximum cable depth, fish-finding luck, and hook capacity. Deeper cable levels let the hook reach farther into the abyss. Luck increases the odds of spawning better fish. Capacity increases how many fish can be brought up in one trip. The Crew tab should sell autonomous helper units such as an Auto Skiff, Escort Drone, and Gold Drone. These helpers should visibly move in the world: one can dive on its own and return fish to the boat, while others orbit the hook, detect nearby targets, chase fish, and bring them back automatically. Their presence should make the water column feel busier and more rewarding over time.

Shape the progression like a sandbox rather than a harsh economy simulator. The budget can be effectively infinite or intentionally non-restrictive, so players are encouraged to experiment freely with upgrades and companions. The fun should come from scaling the system, seeing more fish appear, reaching deeper zones, and watching helper drones multiply the pace of catches. There should be no fail state, no combat, and no level completion requirement—just a smooth endless arcade loop built for relaxation, spectacle, and satisfying accumulation.

Optimize the whole experience for phones and tablets: safe-area padding, large buttons, minimal text clutter, clear depth readout, responsive layout, and touch-safe overlays that do not block the main play space. Keep the tone luminous, rewarding, and slightly adventurous, with ambient loop audio and clean UI animations that make the game feel premium even though the mechanics remain simple and approachable.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## High-level code structure
- Single-file HTML game with embedded CSS and JavaScript.
- Canvas is used for all world rendering: boat, line, hook, fish, helper drones, particles, depth grid, and floating score text.
- DOM overlays handle the meta UI:
  - start screen / launch CTA
  - HUD for budget, depth, and catch count
  - bottom shop panel with gear and crew tabs
  - animated feedback cards for launch and catch streak reactions
- Audio is managed through a lightweight `AudioSys` wrapper that clones short SFX and runs one looping ambience track.
- There is no asset pipeline or module system; game behavior is driven by top-level constants, mutable state objects, and an animation loop.

## Game loop / state model
- Primary global state:
  - `STATE.mode`: `MENU` or `PLAYING`
  - viewport dimensions, time, touch state, shop visibility, active tab
  - sandbox economy fields including infinite money and tracked catch score
- Supporting mutable entities:
  - `boat`
  - `hook` with `IDLE`, `DOWN`, `UP` states and a `caught` list
  - `fishes`
  - `activePets`
  - `particles`
  - `floats`
- Main loop:
  1. `requestAnimationFrame(loop)` computes delta time
  2. `update(dt)` advances systems
  3. `draw()` renders the abyss scene and entities
- Menu mode keeps the boat bobbing and ambient fish moving in the background.
- Play mode enables input-driven hook descent/reel behavior, fish spawning, pet AI, catch processing, and HUD updates.

## Player goals
- Catch as many fish as possible in an endless session.
- Reach deeper zones to access more valuable and visually distinct fish tiers.
- Expand catch capacity and improve luck to encounter stronger fish distributions.
- Recruit helper drones/crew units that automate collection and increase throughput.
- Optimize the descent-and-return rhythm rather than survive or complete levels.

## Interaction pattern
- Core input is extremely simple:
  - hold / press pointer to descend
  - release to reel back upward
- The hook always aligns horizontally with the boat, so play is about timing vertical movement and capacity.
- Meta interaction happens in the always-available deck console:
  - gear tab upgrades depth cable, radar/luck, and hook capacity
  - crew tab adds autonomous helper units
- Start button transitions from title screen to active play and enables audio.

## Core systems
- **Fishing / collection system:** fish collide with the hook while descending; caught fish are stored until the hook returns to the surface.
- **Depth gating system:** max reachable depth scales with the depth upgrade; deeper fish tiers only appear once sufficient depth is unlocked.
- **Spawn quality / luck system:** fish type selection is weighted by current luck level and the unlocked depth ceiling.
- **Capacity system:** hook can hold a limited number of fish before automatically switching to the upward state.
- **Autonomous helper system:** three helper variants exist, with the baby unit diving independently and guard/super drones orbiting and chasing nearby fish.
- **Endless progression sandbox:** upgrades and pets are always purchasable because budget is intentionally infinite; progression is expressive rather than economic.
- **Feedback system:** particles, floating `+1` text, HUD score updates, GIF popups, and SFX reinforce launches and successful catches.
- **Presentation system:** stylized sci-fi abyss theme with glowing gold/teal palette, mobile-safe UI, and a dramatic title card.

## Inferred genre / gameplay shape
- Best understood as an **endless fishing / collection sandbox** with strong overlap with:
  - clicker/incremental design
  - pet/companion automation
  - light inventory/capacity management
  - casual arcade timing
- It is not a strict simulator or survival game.
- Session structure is open-ended: start, repeatedly dive and reel, buy upgrades freely, accumulate catches, and watch the system scale.

## Gameplay heuristic
- Early play: tap and hold to learn the down/up hook rhythm and catch shallow fish.
- Mid play: raise depth and capacity so each dive reaches richer layers and returns with larger hauls.
- Automation phase: add crew drones so catches continue beyond the manual hook path.
- Long-run feel: the player is meant to enjoy spectacle, abundance, and frictionless progression rather than challenge-heavy mastery.

## Confidence notes
- High confidence on the control loop, endless structure, and upgrade/pet systems because they are explicit in code.
- Moderate confidence on intended fantasy framing: UI text says “fish,” while some variable comments reference seals from an earlier concept, so the final theme reads as abyssal fishing with helper drones rather than literal pets.
